definition: Thriving in or tolerant of heavy rainfall; said of plants, fungi, or creatures that flourish precisely where others would drown.
etymology: From Greek ombros, a shower of rain sent by Zeus — cognate with the storm-god's own wet moods — plus philos, loving. Greek naturalists used ombros for the kind of drenching rain that soaks the uplands in autumn; attach the lover's suffix and you have a word that makes fondness of a flood.
usage: Late October hedgerows fill with ombrophilous mosses plumped to brilliance, every stone and rotting post suddenly furred with the green that only arrives when the sky gives up pretending it will stay dry.
